outline.chapter_title: Introduction: The Challenge of Aligning Language Models
outline.description: Large-scale unsupervised language models trained on vast corpora of internet text have demonstrated remarkable capabilities, acquiring broad world knowledge and sophisticated reasoning skills. However, the very nature of their training—learning to predict the next token in sequences generated by humans with diverse goals, priorities, and skill levels—creates a fundamental misalignment between what the model knows and how it behaves. While an unsupervised model may possess the knowledge to identify a common programming error or recognize a widespread scientific misconception, it lacks the inherent mechanism to prioritize high-quality, safe, or helpful responses over mediocre or incorrect ones. outline.chapter_title: The DPO Algorithm: Formulation and Mechanics
outline.description: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) has long been the standard paradigm for aligning large language models with human values. However, the traditional RLHF pipeline is notoriously complex, requiring the training of a separate reward model followed by a delicate reinforcement learning optimization loop, often utilizing algorithms like Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). This process involves sampling from the language model during training, managing multiple neural networks simultaneously, and tuning a vast array of hyperparameters, leading to instability and high computational costs.
